full_judgment:
7. Mr. Abul Kalam Mainuddin, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the plaintiff opposite party No. 1 on the other hand, submits that the defendant No. 8 failed to prove himself as even a lessee, nor he having any legal interest in the suit property, could maintain even the instant application under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure inasmuch as the Government being already a party in the suit, the Government could, if it liked, move the superior court. He further argued that in presence of the Government, even the custodian of the vested property ie defendant No. 2 is also nobody in the case and as such, the appeal preferred by either defendant No. 2 or defendant No. 8 was not maintainable in the eye of law. He next submitted that the plaintiff is entitled to get relief in the suit of at least two courts. Firstly being gifted with the suit property by Reazuddin, the vendee of the deed of agreement of sale executed by defendant No. 1, the plaintiff had locus standi to file and maintain the suit for specific performance of contract in his favour. Secondly, being one of the admitted heirs-in-interest of late Reazuddin Mullik recipient of the deed of agreement of sale executed by the defendant No. 1 he could as well, as heir also maintain the suit and in view of the solenama executed by pro-defendant Nos. 4-7, other co-sharers who are successor-in-interest of the predecessor Reazuddin, the plaintiff was absolutely entitled to get the relief sought for by him in the suit. He contended that considering the facts and circumstances and the evidence on record the trial Court passed the judgment and decree in favour of the plaintiff and the lower appellate Court in its turn considering the facts and circumstances revealed in the case affirmed the aforesaid judgment and decree passed by the trial Court on the basis of materials on record. He, therefore, submitted that there being no error in the decision and moreso no failure of justice being occasioned the defendant No. 8 petitioner the Rule is liable to be discharged. 

 9. As stated above in support of case of the respective parties the trial Court recorded the evidence of the witnesses. It appears that 4 witnesses were examined on behalf of the plaintiff opposite party No. 1 They proved the execution of deed of agreement and also the fact of gift in favour of the plaintiff, witnesses on behalf of the defendant No. 2 and defendant No. 8 were also examined in the suit. Witnesses on behalf of the pro-defendant 4-7 who being heirs of late Reazuddin deposed as to the deed of agreement for sale executed in favour of the predecessor of the plaintiff and also iterating the fact of gift of the suit property in favour of the plaintiff by their predecessor Reazuddin and they also proved the solenama executed by them in favour of the plaintiff categorically stating that the plaintiff is thus entitled to the suit property. It is also noticed that on the basis of the materials including the evidence on record the trial Court found all the issues in favour of the plaintiff and decreed the suit.
